elements.evidence: Section 5.4 expressly provides that “IBM may terminate this Agreement, any Product Attachment, or any Purchase Order for its convenience.”

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience requires thirty (30) days’ notice.
Customer’s termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: Section 5.4 expressly requires “prior written notice to MSL.”

elements.element: Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees following termination for convenience.
elements.evidence: MSL must “refund to IBM any amounts prepaid by IBM for the period after the effective date of termination,” which operatively refunds the unused portion of prepaid amounts.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 5.4 states that “MSL shall have no right to terminate this Agreement, any Product Attachment, or any Purchase Order for convenience during the term.”
Section 5.4 expressly grants IBM a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience requires 60–90 days’ notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires only thirty (30) days’ notice, not notice within the fallback range of 60–90 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three months’ fees.
elements.evidence: Section 5.4 permits termination “without payment of any termination penalty or early termination charge,” so the applicable fee is zero. Cost reimbursements preserved elsewhere are not identified as an early-termination fee.
Although Section 5.4 bars MSL from terminating during the term, the renewal provision permits “either Party” to give notice of its intent to terminate at a term boundary.

elements.element: Vendor may exercise its termination-for-convenience right only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 5.4 bars MSL from terminating for convenience “during the term,” while the existing renewal provision allows either party to terminate through non-renewal at the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor’s end-of-term termination for convenience requires ninety (90) days’ notice.
elements.evidence: The renewal provision requires six (6) months’ written notice, not ninety (90) days’ notice.

result.reason: The operative language fully satisfies the preferred position: IBM has a 30-day written termination-for-convenience right, receives the unused portion of prepaid amounts, and MSL cannot terminate for convenience during the term. The fallback is not independently satisfied because IBM’s notice period is 30 rather than 60–90 days and MSL’s end-of-term notice period is six months rather than 90 days. The redline is not minimal and does not preserve unrelated commercial terms because it adds an unrelated Parts-pricing subsection, expands the right to Product Attachments and partial terminations, and includes malformed drafting such as a dangling “b),” “[＊],” and “Apppendix.”
